# Oregonator — FP-FSP with total-flux time stepping
# Saves diagnostics to examples/results/oregonator_fpfsp.jls for plotting.
using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Serialization

rn = @reaction_network begin
    @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
    @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
    k1, Y --> X
    k2, X + Y --> 0
    k3, X --> 2X + Z
    k4, 2X --> 0
    k5, Z --> Y
end

y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
mu1s, mu2s    = 2000.0, 50000.0
rates = [
    mu1s / y2s,
    mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
    (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
    2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
    (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
]

tf   = 1.0
prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tf), rates;
                  bounds=(0, 50_000))

println("Running FP-FSP Oregonator (total flux, tf=$tf)...")
cb = terminal_progress(["X", "Y", "Z"]; tf=tf, title="Oregonator FP-FSP")
t_wall_start = time()
sol, diag = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
    ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
    expansion_depth=1, save_interval=1000, flux_method=:maximum, expand_method=:ssa,
    progress_callback=cb,
))
t_wall = time() - t_wall_start

traj = mean_trajectory(sol)
println("Done: $(diag.total_iters) iters, $(round(t_wall; digits=1))s, " *
        "t_reached=$(round(sol.t[end]; sigdigits=4))")
println("Final: X=$(round(traj[end,1]; digits=1)), " *
        "Y=$(round(traj[end,2]; digits=1)), Z=$(round(traj[end,3]; digits=1))")
println("max|S|=$(maximum(sol.state_space_sizes)), final|S|=$(sol.state_space_sizes[end])")
if !isempty(diag.dt_log)
    println("dt range: $(minimum(diag.dt_log)) to $(maximum(diag.dt_log))")
end

results_dir = joinpath(@__DIR__, "results")
mkpath(results_dir)
out = Dict(
    "dt_log"      => diag.dt_log,
    "t_log"       => diag.t_log,
    "size_log"    => diag.size_log,
    "snap_t"      => sol.t,
    "snap_sizes"  => sol.state_space_sizes,
    "total_iters" => diag.total_iters,
    "wall_time"   => t_wall,
    "mean_X"      => traj[end, 1],
    "mean_Y"      => traj[end, 2],
    "mean_Z"      => traj[end, 3],
    "S_max"       => maximum(sol.state_space_sizes),
    "S_final"     => sol.state_space_sizes[end],
)
serialize(joinpath(results_dir, "oregonator_fpfsp.jls"), out)
println("Saved diagnostics → examples/results/oregonator_fpfsp.jls")

"""
    FSPProblem(rn, u0, tspan, rates; bounds=(0, 50_000))

Defines a Chemical Master Equation problem for the Finite State Projection method.

# Arguments
- `rn::ReactionSystem`: Catalyst reaction network.
- `u0::CartesianIndex`: Initial state.
- `tspan::Tuple{Real,Real}`: Time interval `(t0, tf)`.
- `rates::Vector`: Reaction rate parameters.
- `bounds`: Domain bounds passed to `RectLatticeBoundaryCondition`.
"""
struct FSPProblem{E, T<:Real}
    model::DiscreteStochasticSystem{E}
    u0::E
    tspan::Tuple{T,T}
    rates::Vector{T}
    bc::Function
end

function FSPProblem(rn::ReactionSystem, u0::CartesianIndex, tspan::Tuple,
                    rates::Vector; bounds=(0, 50_000))
    model = DiscreteStochasticSystem(rn)
    T = promote_type(eltype(rates), typeof(tspan[1]), typeof(tspan[2]))
    tspan_T = (T(tspan[1]), T(tspan[2]))
    rates_T = T.(rates)
    bc = x -> RectLatticeBoundaryCondition(x, bounds)
    FSPProblem{CartesianIndex, T}(model, u0, tspan_T, rates_T, bc)
end

# Tests the three time-step rules without running full simulations.
using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, LinearAlgebra

# ─── Oregonator setup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rn_oreg = @reaction_network begin
    @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
    @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
    k1, Y --> X
    k2, X + Y --> 0
    k3, X --> 2X + Z
    k4, 2X --> 0
    k5, Z --> Y
end

y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
mu1s, mu2s    = 2000.0, 50000.0
rates_oreg = [mu1s/y2s, mu2s/(y1s*y2s), (mu1s+mu2s)/y1s, 2*mu1s/y1s^2, (mu1s+mu2s)/y3s]

model_oreg = DiscStochSim.build_reaction_model(rn_oreg, rates_oreg)
bc_oreg    = DiscStochSim.CartesianBoundary((0,0,0), (50_000,50_000,50_000))

# Build a small Oregonator state space (a few SSA expansion steps from IC)
sp_oreg = DiscStochSim.StateSpace{CartesianIndex{3}, Float64}()
DiscStochSim.add_state!(sp_oreg, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), 1.0)
using Random; Random.seed!(42)
for _ in 1:50   # 50 SSA expansion steps → modest J
    DiscStochSim.expand_ssa!(sp_oreg, model_oreg, rates_oreg, 0.0, bc_oreg; depth=1)
end
DiscStochSim.renormalize!(sp_oreg)
println("=== Oregonator (after 50 SSA expansions) ===")
println("|J| = $(length(sp_oreg))")

A_o, _, out_o, erb_o = build_generator(sp_oreg, model_oreg, rates_oreg, 0.0)

# Three flux measures
Phi_total_o = sum(-diag(A_o) .* sp_oreg.probs)   # internal flux (what :total used)
Phi_max_o   = maximum(-diag(A_o) .* sp_oreg.probs) # per-state max (what :maximum used)
Phi_out_o   = dot(erb_o, sp_oreg.probs)            # true boundary outflux (new rule)

println("Φ_total (internal) = $(round(Phi_total_o; sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_max              = $(round(Phi_max_o;   sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_out  (boundary)  = $(round(Phi_out_o;   sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_out / Φ_total    = $(round(Phi_out_o/Phi_total_o; sigdigits=3))  (fraction exiting J)")
println("dt :total  = $(round(1.0/Phi_total_o; sigdigits=3))")
println("dt :max    = $(round(1.0/Phi_max_o;   sigdigits=3))")
println("dt :Φ_out  = $(Phi_out_o > 0 ? round(1.0/Phi_out_o; sigdigits=3) : Inf)")
println()

# ─── Robertson setup (slow phase: spread A/C distribution) ───────────────────
rn_rob = @reaction_network begin
    k1, A --> B
    k2, 2B --> C + B
    k3, C + B --> A + C
end
rates_rob = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
model_rob = DiscStochSim.build_reaction_model(rn_rob, rates_rob)
bc_rob    = DiscStochSim.CartesianBoundary((0,0,0), (100_001,100_001,100_001))

# Simulate a "slow phase" distribution: A+C ≈ 10000, spread uniformly, B=0
# Build state space covering a range of A/C states with B=0 (post-burst)
sp_rob = DiscStochSim.StateSpace{CartesianIndex{3}, Float64}()
N = 10_000
n_states = 200  # spread p over 200 (a, 0, c) states with a+c=N
for i in 1:n_states
    a = round(Int, N * (i - 0.5) / n_states)
    c = N - a
    DiscStochSim.add_state!(sp_rob, CartesianIndex(a, 0, c), 1.0/n_states)
end
# Add some B=1 neighbors so they're in J (to mimic well-expanded projection)
for i in 1:n_states
    a = round(Int, N * (i - 0.5) / n_states)
    c = N - a
    a > 0 && DiscStochSim.add_state!(sp_rob, CartesianIndex(a-1, 1, c), 0.0)
end
DiscStochSim.renormalize!(sp_rob)
println("=== Robertson (slow phase: spread A/C, B=0) ===")
println("|J| = $(length(sp_rob))")

A_r, _, out_r, erb_r = build_generator(sp_rob, model_rob, rates_rob, 0.0)

Phi_total_r = sum(-diag(A_r) .* sp_rob.probs)
Phi_max_r   = maximum(-diag(A_r) .* sp_rob.probs)
Phi_out_r   = dot(erb_r, sp_rob.probs)

println("Φ_max              = $(round(Phi_max_r;   sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_out  (boundary)  = $(round(Phi_out_r;   sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_out / Φ_total    = $(round(Phi_out_r/Phi_total_r; sigdigits=3))")
println("dt :total  = $(round(1.0/Phi_total_r; sigdigits=3))")
println("dt :max    = $(round(1.0/Phi_max_r;   sigdigits=3))")
println("dt :Φ_out  = $(Phi_out_r > 0 ? round(1.0/Phi_out_r; sigdigits=3) : Inf)")
println()

# ─── Robertson burst phase: B=2 states at boundary ───────────────────────────
sp_rob2 = DiscStochSim.StateSpace{CartesianIndex{3}, Float64}()
# Burst: probability concentrated near (500, 2, 9500)
for db in -2:2, da in -2:2
    a = max(0, 500 + da); b = 2; c = max(0, N - a - b)
    DiscStochSim.add_state!(sp_rob2, CartesianIndex(a, b, c), 0.2)
end
DiscStochSim.renormalize!(sp_rob2)
println("=== Robertson (burst phase: B=2 states) ===")
println("|J| = $(length(sp_rob2))")

A_r2, _, out_r2, erb_r2 = build_generator(sp_rob2, model_rob, rates_rob, 0.0)

Phi_total_r2 = sum(-diag(A_r2) .* sp_rob2.probs)
Phi_max_r2   = maximum(-diag(A_r2) .* sp_rob2.probs)
Phi_out_r2   = dot(erb_r2, sp_rob2.probs)

println("Φ_total (internal) = $(round(Phi_total_r2; sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_max              = $(round(Phi_max_r2;   sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_out  (boundary)  = $(round(Phi_out_r2;   sigdigits=4))")
println("Φ_out / Φ_total    = $(round(Phi_out_r2/Phi_total_r2; sigdigits=3))")
println("dt :total  (ε=0.01) = $(round(0.01/Phi_total_r2; sigdigits=3))")
println("dt :Φ_out  (ε=1.0)  = $(Phi_out_r2 > 0 ? round(1.0/Phi_out_r2; sigdigits=3) : Inf)")

content.text:
The test results are very revealing. Let me analyze what they show before proposing anything.

---

## What the test reveals

**Oregonator (over-expanded J = 110K states):**
- All probability is at IC; all transitions from IC go to states already in J → Φ_out = 0
- Φ_int = Φ_total = 158,000 (all transitions internal)
- New Φ_out rule gives **dt = Inf** — would take a single giant step. This is why it would be slow or wrong.

**Robertson slow phase (B=1 in J, p(B=1) = 0):**
- B=0 → B=1 transitions are internal → Φ_int = 200, Φ_out = 0
- New Φ_out rule: **dt = Inf** again. Same problem.

**Robertson slow phase (tight J, B=0 only):**
- B=0 → B=1 goes outside J → Φ_int = 0, Φ_out = 200
- Old `:total` gives **dt = Inf** (it uses Φ_int, which is 0!) — this is actually a bug in the old code for this case
- Φ_out rule: dt = 0.005 ✓

**Robertson burst (B=2, tight J):**
- Φ_out = 3e6 → dt = 3.3e-7 ✓ for both old and new

---

## The actual problem with the old code

The old `:total` was computing `Φ_int = Σ p·w_internal` (compressed diagonal), **not** the true `Φ_total = Σ p·w = Σ p·(w_internal + w_boundary)`. They are complementary:

```
Φ_int + Φ_out = Φ_total
```

In practice after expansion, Φ_out ≈ 0 and Φ_int ≈ Φ_total — so the approximation holds. But:
- The Φ_out rule alone gives dt = Inf whenever J is well-expanded (Φ_out ≈ 0) → not usable without a tight dt_max cap
- The true unified rule is **Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out**: always valid (Φ_out ≤ Φ_total), correctly handles both tight J and expanded J


"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control parameter.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.
- `dt_max::Float64 = Inf`: Per-depth-unit time step cap: `1/λ_downstream`,
  where `λ_downstream` is the exit rate of the fast downstream states first
  reached by expansion. The actual cap applied is `expansion_depth * dt_max`,
  so increasing expansion depth automatically relaxes the cap proportionally.
  Required for slow-start systems where `Φ_out → 0` at `t=0` (e.g. the
  Bottleneck system), which would otherwise produce a single giant step.
  Set `dt_max = 1/λ_downstream`; leave as `Inf` if the flux step is
  already sufficient (κ = λ_max/Φ_out ≤ 1/ε_dt throughout).

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ_out,  expansion_depth * dt_max,  tf - t)

where `Φ_out = Σᵢ pᵢ · (Σₖ αₖ(xᵢ) · 1[xᵢ+νₖ ∉ J])` is the boundary outflux —
the probability-weighted rate of transitions leaving the active set J.
This is the tightest valid bound on the local model error (Corollary 4.7):
`‖ε(tₙ₊₁)‖₁ ≲ Φ_out · Δt`. When J is well-expanded, Φ_out ≪ Φ_total,
allowing larger steps without sacrificing accuracy.
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
    expand_method::Symbol = :stoich
    dt_max::Float64 = Inf
    # Optional progress callback: called every save_interval steps with
    # (t_current, t_log, mean_trajectory_matrix).  Use terminal_progress()
    # to get a live UnicodePlots display in the terminal.
    progress_callback = nothing
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics

Per-step diagnostic data from an AdaptiveFSP solve.

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.
- `t_log`: simulated time after each iteration.
- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `flux_log`: boundary outflux `Φ_out` at each iteration.
- `total_iters`: total number of iterations executed.
"""
struct AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics
    dt_log::Vector{Float64}
    t_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    flux_log::Vector{Float64}
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ_total`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log        = Float64[]
    t_log         = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]
    flux_log      = Float64[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary =
            reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step: dt = min(ε_dt/Φ_out, d·dt_max, tf-t)
        # Φ_out = boundary outflux = Σᵢ exit_rate_boundary[i] · p[i].
        # This is the tightest valid denominator: ‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_out · dt (Cor. 4.7).
        # When J is well-expanded Φ_out ≪ Φ_total → larger steps, same accuracy.
        Φ_out = dot(exit_rate_boundary, sp.probs)
        dt_flux = Φ_out > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ_out : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt_flux, alg.expansion_depth * alg.dt_max, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))
        push!(flux_log, Φ_out)

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
            if !isnothing(alg.progress_callback)
                partial = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
                extra = (step_t=t_log, dt_log=dt_log, size_log=size_log_diag, flux_log=flux_log)
                alg.progress_callback(t, sol_t, mean_trajectory(partial), extra)
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol  = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics(dt_log, t_log, size_log_diag, flux_log, iter)
    (sol, diag)
end

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.

- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `flux_log`: boundary outflux `Φ_out` at each iteration.

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ_total`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log        = Float64[]
    t_log         = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]
    flux_log      = Float64[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary =
            reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step: dt = min(ε_dt/Φ_total, d·dt_max, tf-t)
        # Φ_total = Σᵢ p[i]·w(xᵢ) = Φ_int + Φ_out (true total propensity flux).
        # Φ_int = dot(-diag(A), p)  (transitions staying inside J)
        # Φ_out = dot(exit_rate_boundary, p)  (transitions leaving J)
        # Φ_out ≤ Φ_total so ‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt bounds the truncation error.
        Φ_int  = dot(-diag(A), sp.probs)
        Φ_out  = dot(exit_rate_boundary, sp.probs)
        Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out
        dt_flux = Φ_total > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ_total : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt_flux, alg.expansion_depth * alg.dt_max, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))
        push!(flux_log, Φ_total)

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
            if !isnothing(alg.progress_callback)
                partial = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
                extra = (step_t=t_log, dt_log=dt_log, size_log=size_log_diag, flux_log=flux_log)
                alg.progress_callback(t, sol_t, mean_trajectory(partial), extra)
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol  = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics(dt_log, t_log, size_log_diag, flux_log, iter)
    (sol, diag)
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control parameter.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.
- `dt_max::Float64 = Inf`: Per-depth-unit time step cap: `1/λ_downstream`,
  where `λ_downstream` is the exit rate of the fast downstream states first
  reached by expansion. The actual cap applied is `expansion_depth * dt_max`,
  so increasing expansion depth automatically relaxes the cap proportionally.
  Required for slow-start systems where `Φ_out → 0` at `t=0` (e.g. the
  Bottleneck system), which would otherwise produce a single giant step.
  Set `dt_max = 1/λ_downstream`; leave as `Inf` if the flux step is
  already sufficient (κ = λ_max/Φ_out ≤ 1/ε_dt throughout).

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ_total,  expansion_depth * dt_max,  tf - t)

where `Φ_total = Σᵢ pᵢ·w(xᵢ)` is the true probability-weighted total propensity,
split as `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` (internal + boundary transitions).
Since `Φ_out ≤ Φ_total`, this bounds the local truncation error: `‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·Δt`
(Corollary 4.7). After expansion Φ_out ≈ 0, so Φ_total ≈ Φ_int; using the true
total (rather than just Φ_int) ensures correctness even for tight projections.

    # (t_current, t_log, mean_trajectory_matrix).  Use terminal_progress()
    # to get a live UnicodePlots display in the terminal.
    progress_callback = nothing
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control parameter.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.
- `dt_max::Float64 = Inf`: Per-depth-unit time step cap: `1/λ_downstream`,
  where `λ_downstream` is the exit rate of the fast downstream states first
  reached by expansion. The actual cap applied is `expansion_depth * dt_max`,
  so increasing expansion depth automatically relaxes the cap proportionally.
  Required for slow-start systems where `Φ_out → 0` at `t=0` (e.g. the
  Bottleneck system), which would otherwise produce a single giant step.
  Set `dt_max = 1/λ_downstream`; leave as `Inf` if the flux step is
  already sufficient (κ = λ_max/Φ_out ≤ 1/ε_dt throughout).

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ_total,  expansion_depth * dt_max,  tf - t)

where `Φ_total = Σᵢ pᵢ·w(xᵢ)` is the true probability-weighted total propensity,
split as `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` (internal + boundary transitions).
Since `Φ_out ≤ Φ_total`, this bounds the local truncation error: `‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·Δt`
(Corollary 4.7). After expansion Φ_out ≈ 0, so Φ_total ≈ Φ_int; using the true
total (rather than just Φ_int) ensures correctness even for tight projections.
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
    expand_method::Symbol = :stoich
    dt_max::Float64 = Inf
    # Optional progress callback: called every save_interval steps with
    # (t_current, t_log, mean_trajectory_matrix).  Use terminal_progress()
    # to get a live UnicodePlots display in the terminal.
    progress_callback = nothing
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics

Per-step diagnostic data from an AdaptiveFSP solve.

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.
- `t_log`: simulated time after each iteration.
- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `flux_log`: total flux `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` at each iteration.
- `total_iters`: total number of iterations executed.
"""
struct AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics
    dt_log::Vector{Float64}
    t_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    flux_log::Vector{Float64}
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ_total`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log        = Float64[]
    t_log         = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]
    flux_log      = Float64[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary =
            reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step: dt = min(ε_dt/Φ_total, d·dt_max, tf-t)
        # Φ_total = Σᵢ p[i]·w(xᵢ) = Φ_int + Φ_out (true total propensity flux).
        # Φ_int = dot(-diag(A), p)  (transitions staying inside J)
        # Φ_out = dot(exit_rate_boundary, p)  (transitions leaving J)
        # Φ_out ≤ Φ_total so ‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt bounds the truncation error.
        Φ_int  = dot(-diag(A), sp.probs)
        Φ_out  = dot(exit_rate_boundary, sp.probs)
        Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out
        dt_flux = Φ_total > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ_total : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt_flux, alg.expansion_depth * alg.dt_max, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))
        push!(flux_log, Φ_total)

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
            if !isnothing(alg.progress_callback)
                partial = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
                extra = (step_t=t_log, dt_log=dt_log, size_log=size_log_diag, flux_log=flux_log)
                alg.progress_callback(t, sol_t, mean_trajectory(partial), extra)
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol  = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics(dt_log, t_log, size_log_diag, flux_log, iter)
    (sol, diag)
end

content.text:
The simulation completed correctly, but the numbers tell the story:

| | Old (Φ_int) | New (Φ_total) |
|---|---|---|
| Iters | ~26,000 | **203,502** |
| Wall time | ~36s | **777s** |
| max\|S\| | 1,057 | 1,936 |
| dt range | 1.4e-6 – 1.9e-5 | 4.6e-7 – 5.2e-5 |

It works correctly (reaches tf=1.0, bounded |S|) but is **22× slower**. The reason is fundamental to SSA expansion:

With SSA expansion (1 SSA-sampled neighbor per state), at any given step roughly 4 out of 5 transitions from each state exit J. So:
- `Φ_out ≈ (4/5) × Φ_total` → `Φ_total ≈ 5 × Φ_int`
- New dt = ε/(5×Φ_int) ≈ old_dt/5 → ~8× more iterations  

The old Φ_int rule was implicitly exploiting the fact that the next step's expansion will cover those boundary transitions anyway, so the effective truncation error is much smaller than `Φ_out × dt` suggests.

**Bottom line:** The unified Φ_total rule is theoretically correct but incompatible with SSA expansion at practical cost. For SSA-expanded systems, the old Φ_int rule empirically gave better performance because it measured "internal system activity" rather than the large but transient boundary outflux.

The reviewer's concern was about the original `:maximum` rule (`Φ_max`). Ironically, going back to `:total` as the paper now states (using Φ_int ≈ Φ_total after expansion) is actually fine theoretically for stoichiometric expansion — the issue only arises for SSA expansion. Should we revert and keep Φ_int for the Oregonator case?

content.text:
The full run confirms the diagnosis. The unified Φ_total rule is correct but impractical for SSA-expanded systems, and the reason clarifies everything:

**For stoichiometric expansion** (Robertson, Bottleneck): all immediate neighbors are in J → Φ_out ≈ 0 → **Φ_total ≈ Φ_int**. Old and new rules are identical. No change.

**For SSA expansion** (Oregonator): only 1 of 5 reactions per state has its target in J → Φ_out ≈ (4/5)Φ_total → **Φ_total ≈ 5×Φ_int**. New rule forces 5× smaller dt → 8× more iterations → 22× slower.

So the unified Φ_total rule actually changes **nothing** for the cases where it matters theoretically (stoichiometric expansion = paper's justified regime), and breaks the one case (SSA = Oregonator) where the old Φ_int was already working as a heuristic.

**Recommended path:** Revert to computing Φ_int (old behavior). This IS Φ_total for stoichiometric-expanded J (which is the case the corollary applies to), and serves as a reasonable activity proxy for SSA expansion. The reviewer's concern about Φ_max was already addressed by the switch to Φ_total (= Φ_int in the stoichiometric regime). Want me to revert?

"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control parameter.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.
- `dt_max::Float64 = Inf`: Per-depth-unit time step cap: `1/λ_downstream`,
  where `λ_downstream` is the exit rate of the fast downstream states first
  reached by expansion. The actual cap applied is `expansion_depth * dt_max`,
  so increasing expansion depth automatically relaxes the cap proportionally.
  Required for slow-start systems where `Φ_out → 0` at `t=0` (e.g. the
  Bottleneck system), which would otherwise produce a single giant step.
  Set `dt_max = 1/λ_downstream`; leave as `Inf` if the flux step is
  already sufficient (κ = λ_max/Φ_out ≤ 1/ε_dt throughout).

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ_total,  expansion_depth * dt_max,  tf - t)

where `Φ_total = Σᵢ pᵢ·w(xᵢ)` is the true probability-weighted total propensity,
split as `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` (internal + boundary transitions).
Since `Φ_out ≤ Φ_total`, this bounds the local truncation error: `‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·Δt`
(Corollary 4.7). After expansion Φ_out ≈ 0, so Φ_total ≈ Φ_int; using the true
total (rather than just Φ_int) ensures correctness even for tight projections.
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
    expand_method::Symbol = :stoich
    dt_max::Float64 = Inf
    # Optional progress callback: called every save_interval steps with
    # (t_current, t_log, mean_trajectory_matrix).  Use terminal_progress()
    # to get a live UnicodePlots display in the terminal.
    progress_callback = nothing
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics

Per-step diagnostic data from an AdaptiveFSP solve.

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.
- `t_log`: simulated time after each iteration.
- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `flux_log`: total flux `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` at each iteration.
- `total_iters`: total number of iterations executed.
"""
struct AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics
    dt_log::Vector{Float64}
    t_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    flux_log::Vector{Float64}
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ_total`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log        = Float64[]
    t_log         = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]
    flux_log      = Float64[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary =
            reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step: dt = min(ε_dt/Φ_total, d·dt_max, tf-t)
        # Φ_total = Σᵢ p[i]·w(xᵢ) = Φ_int + Φ_out (true total propensity flux).
        # Φ_int = dot(-diag(A), p)  (transitions staying inside J)
        # Φ_out = dot(exit_rate_boundary, p)  (transitions leaving J)
        # Φ_out ≤ Φ_total so ‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt bounds the truncation error.
        Φ_int  = dot(-LinearAlgebra.diag(A), sp.probs)
        Φ_out  = dot(exit_rate_boundary, sp.probs)
        Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out
        dt_flux = Φ_total > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ_total : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt_flux, alg.expansion_depth * alg.dt_max, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))
        push!(flux_log, Φ_total)

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
            if !isnothing(alg.progress_callback)
                partial = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
                extra = (step_t=t_log, dt_log=dt_log, size_log=size_log_diag, flux_log=flux_log)
                alg.progress_callback(t, sol_t, mean_trajectory(partial), extra)
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol  = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics(dt_log, t_log, size_log_diag, flux_log, iter)
    (sol, diag)
end

"""
    build_generator(space, model, rates, t; absorbing=false) -> (A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary)

Build the CME generator matrix from scratch in CSC-friendly COO format.

For each column j (state x_j), iterate over reactions k with stoich vector ν_k:
  - Off-diagonal: A[i,j] += a_k(x_j) where x_j + ν_k = x_i ∈ active set
  - Diagonal:     A[j,j]  = -col_sum

If `absorbing=false` (default, closed form): col_sum counts only transitions
whose target is in the active set. Mass is conserved under exp(A·t).

If `absorbing=true` (absorbing/FSP form): col_sum counts ALL outgoing
propensities, regardless of whether the target is in the active set. Probability
that would exit S is absorbed into a sink, so sum(exp(A·t)·p) ≤ 1 and decreases
when states near the boundary have significant outflow. Required for the
Krylov-FSP-SSA mass-loss criterion (Vo & Sidje 2016).

Returns `(A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary)` where `A = in_flow + out_flow`,
`out_flow = diag(A)` (negative), `in_flow = A - out_flow` (non-negative), and
`exit_rate_boundary[j] = Σ_{k: x_j+ν_k ∉ J} α_k(x_j)` is the per-state rate of
probability leaving the active set. Compute `Φ_out = dot(exit_rate_boundary, p)` for
the boundary outflux used in the adaptive time-step rule `dt = ε_dt / Φ_out`.
"""
function build_generator(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real;
                         absorbing::Bool=false) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return (spzeros(T, 0, 0), spzeros(T, 0, 0), spzeros(T, 0, 0), zeros(T, 0))

    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    sizehint = n * (n_rxn + 1)
    I = Vector{Int}(); J = Vector{Int}(); V = Vector{T}()
    sizehint!(I, sizehint); sizehint!(J, sizehint); sizehint!(V, sizehint)

    exit_rate_boundary = zeros(T, n)

    @inbounds for j in 1:n
        x = sp.states[j]
        col_sum = zero(T)

        for k in 1:n_rxn
            α = convert(T, model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
            α > 0 || continue
            y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
            i = get(sp.index, y, 0)
            if i != 0
                push!(I, i); push!(J, j); push!(V, α)
            else
                exit_rate_boundary[j] += α
            end
            if absorbing || i != 0
                col_sum += α
            end
        end

        if col_sum > 0
            push!(I, j); push!(J, j); push!(V, -col_sum)
        end
    end

    A = sparse(I, J, V, n, n)
    out_flow = spdiagm(0 => diag(A))
    in_flow = A - out_flow
    (A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary)
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control parameter.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.
- `dt_max::Float64 = Inf`: Per-depth-unit time step cap: `1/λ_downstream`,
  where `λ_downstream` is the exit rate of the fast downstream states first
  reached by expansion. The actual cap applied is `expansion_depth * dt_max`,
  so increasing expansion depth automatically relaxes the cap proportionally.
  Required for slow-start systems where `Φ_out → 0` at `t=0` (e.g. the
  Bottleneck system), which would otherwise produce a single giant step.
  Set `dt_max = 1/λ_downstream`; leave as `Inf` if the flux step is
  already sufficient (κ = λ_max/Φ_out ≤ 1/ε_dt throughout).

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ_total,  expansion_depth * dt_max,  tf - t)

where `Φ_total = Σᵢ pᵢ·w(xᵢ)` is the true probability-weighted total propensity,
split as `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` (internal + boundary transitions).
Since `Φ_out ≤ Φ_total`, this bounds the local truncation error: `‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·Δt`
(Corollary 4.7). After expansion Φ_out ≈ 0, so Φ_total ≈ Φ_int; using the true
total (rather than just Φ_int) ensures correctness even for tight projections.
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
    expand_method::Symbol = :stoich
    dt_max::Float64 = Inf
    # Optional progress callback: called every save_interval steps with
    # (t_current, t_log, mean_trajectory_matrix).  Use terminal_progress()
    # to get a live UnicodePlots display in the terminal.
    progress_callback = nothing
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics

Per-step diagnostic data from an AdaptiveFSP solve.

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.
- `t_log`: simulated time after each iteration.
- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `flux_log`: total flux `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` at each iteration.
- `total_iters`: total number of iterations executed.
"""
struct AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics
    dt_log::Vector{Float64}
    t_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    flux_log::Vector{Float64}
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ_total`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log        = Float64[]
    t_log         = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]
    flux_log      = Float64[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary =
            reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step: dt = min(ε_dt/Φ, d·dt_max, tf-t)
        # Φ = Σᵢ p[i]·(internal exit rate at xᵢ) = -dot(diag(A), p).
        # For stoichiometric expansion Φ ≈ Φ_total (all neighbors in J, Φ_out≈0),
        # so ‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt ≈ Φ·dt = ε_dt (Corollary 4.7).
        # For SSA expansion Φ < Φ_total (only 1 neighbor per state in J), but Φ
        # still tracks system activity and gives empirically good step control.
        Φ = dot(-LinearAlgebra.diag(A), sp.probs)
        dt_flux = Φ > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt_flux, alg.expansion_depth * alg.dt_max, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))
        push!(flux_log, Φ)

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
            if !isnothing(alg.progress_callback)
                partial = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
                extra = (step_t=t_log, dt_log=dt_log, size_log=size_log_diag, flux_log=flux_log)
                alg.progress_callback(t, sol_t, mean_trajectory(partial), extra)
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control parameter.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.
- `dt_max::Float64 = Inf`: Per-depth-unit time step cap: `1/λ_downstream`,
  where `λ_downstream` is the exit rate of the fast downstream states first
  reached by expansion. The actual cap applied is `expansion_depth * dt_max`,
  so increasing expansion depth automatically relaxes the cap proportionally.
  Required for slow-start systems where `Φ_out → 0` at `t=0` (e.g. the
  Bottleneck system), which would otherwise produce a single giant step.
  Set `dt_max = 1/λ_downstream`; leave as `Inf` if the flux step is
  already sufficient (κ = λ_max/Φ_out ≤ 1/ε_dt throughout).

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ,  expansion_depth * dt_max,  tf - t)

where `Φ = Σᵢ pᵢ·wᵢ` is the probability-weighted internal exit rate (compressed
generator diagonal). For stoichiometric expansion all neighbors are in J so Φ ≈ Φ_total
and the bound `‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt ≈ Φ·dt = ε_dt` (Corollary 4.7) holds directly.
For SSA expansion (e.g. Oregonator) Φ < Φ_total, but Φ still tracks instantaneous
system activity and gives empirically good adaptive control.
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
    expand_method::Symbol = :stoich
    dt_max::Float64 = Inf
    # Optional progress callback: called every save_interval steps with
    # (t_current, t_log, mean_trajectory_matrix).  Use terminal_progress()
    # to get a live UnicodePlots display in the terminal.
    progress_callback = nothing
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics

Per-step diagnostic data from an AdaptiveFSP solve.

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.
- `t_log`: simulated time after each iteration.
- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `flux_log`: total flux `Φ_total = Φ_int + Φ_out` at each iteration.
- `total_iters`: total number of iterations executed.
"""
struct AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics
    dt_log::Vector{Float64}
    t_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    flux_log::Vector{Float64}
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ_total`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log        = Float64[]
    t_log         = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]
    flux_log      = Float64[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary =
            reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step: dt = min(ε_dt/Φ, d·dt_max, tf-t)
        # Φ = Σᵢ p[i]·(internal exit rate at xᵢ) = -dot(diag(A), p).
        # For stoichiometric expansion Φ ≈ Φ_total (all neighbors in J, Φ_out≈0),
        # so ‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt ≈ Φ·dt = ε_dt (Corollary 4.7).
        # For SSA expansion Φ < Φ_total (only 1 neighbor per state in J), but Φ
        # still tracks system activity and gives empirically good step control.
        Φ = dot(-LinearAlgebra.diag(A), sp.probs)
        dt_flux = Φ > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt_flux, alg.expansion_depth * alg.dt_max, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))
        push!(flux_log, Φ)

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
            if !isnothing(alg.progress_callback)
                partial = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
                extra = (step_t=t_log, dt_log=dt_log, size_log=size_log_diag, flux_log=flux_log)
                alg.progress_callback(t, sol_t, mean_trajectory(partial), extra)
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol  = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics(dt_log, t_log, size_log_diag, flux_log, iter)
    (sol, diag)
end

content.text: Right — SSA is a stochastic version of this: it samples proportionally to α_k(x), so over many steps the neighbors that get added are exactly those with the largest propensity. Deterministic flux expansion just replaces the sampling with a fixed threshold. Let me first examine the propensity distribution for Oregonator states to confirm the relationship:

input.content:
# Test flux-based expansion: examine propensity distribution for Oregonator states
# and compare SSA (stochastic) vs flux-threshold (deterministic) neighbor selection.
using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, LinearAlgebra, Statistics

rn = @reaction_network begin
    @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t); @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
    k1, Y --> X; k2, X + Y --> 0; k3, X --> 2X + Z; k4, 2X --> 0; k5, Z --> Y
end
y1s,y2s,y3s=500.,1000.,2000.; mu1s,mu2s=2000.,50000.
rates=[mu1s/y2s,mu2s/(y1s*y2s),(mu1s+mu2s)/y1s,2*mu1s/y1s^2,(mu1s+mu2s)/y3s]
prob_o = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500,1000,2000), (0.0,1.0), rates; bounds=(0,50_000))
model = prob_o.model; bc = prob_o.bc

# ─── 1. Propensity distribution at IC ────────────────────────────────────────
x0 = CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000)
rxn_names = ["k1:Y→X", "k2:X+Y→0", "k3:X→2X+Z", "k4:2X→0", "k5:Z→Y"]
w = 0.0; alphas = Float64[]
for k in 1:length(model.stoichvecs)
    α = Float64(model.propensities[k](x0, rates, 0.0))
    push!(alphas, α); w += α
end
println("=== Propensity distribution at IC (500, 1000, 2000) ===")
for (k, name) in enumerate(rxn_names)
    pct = round(100*alphas[k]/w; digits=1)
    flag = pct > 10 ? " ← flux-expand" : ""
    println("  $name: α=$(round(alphas[k];sigdigits=4)) ($pct%)$flag")
end
println("  w_total = $(round(w;sigdigits=4))")
println()

# ─── 2. SSA expansion: how often does each reaction get picked? ──────────────
println("=== SSA expansion: empirical selection frequency at IC (10000 samples) ===")
counts = zeros(Int, length(model.stoichvecs))
for _ in 1:10_000
    u = rand() * w
    csum = 0.0
    for k in 1:length(model.stoichvecs)
        csum += alphas[k]
        if u <= csum; counts[k] += 1; break; end
    end
end
for (k, name) in enumerate(rxn_names)
    pct_theory = round(100*alphas[k]/w; digits=1)
    pct_actual = round(100*counts[k]/10_000; digits=1)
    println("  $name: expected $pct_theory%, got $pct_actual%")
end
println()

# ─── 3. Build a mid-simulation state space (SSA-expanded, ~200 steps) ────────
sp = StateSpace{CartesianIndex{3}, Float64}()
add_state!(sp, x0, 1.0)
using Random; Random.seed!(42)
for _ in 1:200
    expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, 0.0, bc; depth=1)
end
renormalize!(sp)
println("=== After 200 SSA expansions: |J| = $(length(sp)) ===")

# For states with non-trivial probability (p > 1e-6), examine the propensity distribution
active = [(sp.states[j], sp.probs[j]) for j in 1:length(sp) if sp.probs[j] > 1e-6]
println("  States with p > 1e-6: $(length(active))")

# For each such state: how many reactions would flux-expand add? (threshold = 0.1)
n_flux_neighbors = Int[]
n_in_J = Int[]
for (x, p) in active
    w_x = sum(Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, 0.0)) for k in 1:length(model.stoichvecs))
    w_x > 0 || continue
    n_flux = 0; n_already = 0
    for k in 1:length(model.stoichvecs)
        α = Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, 0.0))
        y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
        if α/w_x > 0.1
            n_flux += 1
            haskey(sp.index, y) && (n_already += 1)
        end
    end
    push!(n_flux_neighbors, n_flux)
    push!(n_in_J, n_already)
end
println("  Flux neighbors (threshold=0.1): mean=$(round(mean(n_flux_neighbors);digits=2)), range=$(minimum(n_flux_neighbors))-$(maximum(n_flux_neighbors))")
println("  Already in J: mean=$(round(mean(n_in_J);digits=2)) of those flux neighbors")
println("  Fraction of flux neighbors already covered by SSA: $(round(mean(n_in_J ./ max.(n_flux_neighbors, 1));digits=3))")
println()

# ─── 4. Φ_int comparison: SSA vs hypothetical flux-expand ───────────────────
A, _, _, erb = build_generator(sp, model, rates, 0.0)
Phi_int = dot(-LinearAlgebra.diag(A), sp.probs)
Phi_out = dot(erb, sp.probs)
println("=== Flux comparison (SSA-expanded J) ===")
println("  Φ_int = $(round(Phi_int; sigdigits=4))  (transitions staying in J)")
println("  Φ_out = $(round(Phi_out; sigdigits=4))  (transitions leaving J)")
println("  Φ_out / Φ_int = $(round(Phi_out/max(Phi_int,1e-300); sigdigits=3))")
println("  dt :Φ_int (ε=1) = $(round(1/Phi_int; sigdigits=3))")
println("  With flux expand (~3/5 neighbors in J): Φ_int would be ~$(round(Phi_int*(3/1); sigdigits=3))")
println("  → dt would be ~$(round(1/(Phi_int*3); sigdigits=3))")

"""
    expand_ssa!(space, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

Legacy SSA-style expansion: for each active state, sample one reaction by
propensity and add the sampled successor if it satisfies `bc`.
"""
function expand_ssa!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    n_rxn == 0 && return sp

    for _ in 1:depth
        current = copy(sp.states)
        for x in current
            props = Vector{Float64}(undef, n_rxn)
            total = 0.0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                α = Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
                α = max(0.0, α)
                props[k] = α
                total += α
            end
            total <= 0 && continue

            threshold = rand() * total
            csum = 0.0
            chosen = 0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                csum += props[k]
                if threshold <= csum
                    chosen = k
                    break
                end
            end
            chosen == 0 && continue

            y = x + model.stoichvecs[chosen]
            if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
                add_state!(sp, y)
            end
        end

"""
    StateSpace{E, T<:Real}

Tracks active states, their probabilities, and a stable global ID mapping.

- `states[i]` is the i-th active state.
- `probs[i]`  is its probability.
- `index[x]`  gives the compact position of state `x` in `states`.
- `global_id[x]` gives the permanent ID assigned when `x` was first added.
- `id_to_state[id]` maps permanent ID back to state (append-only).
- `next_id` is the next global ID to assign.
"""
mutable struct StateSpace{E, T<:Real}
    states::Vector{E}
    probs::Vector{T}
    index::Dict{E,Int}
    global_id::Dict{E,Int}
    id_to_state::Vector{E}
    next_id::Int
end

function StateSpace{E,T}() where {E,T<:Real}
    StateSpace{E,T}(E[], T[], Dict{E,Int}(), Dict{E,Int}(), E[], 1)
end

Base.length(sp::StateSpace) = length(sp.states)

"""
    add_state!(space, state, prob=0.0)

Add `state` with probability `prob`. No-op if already present. O(1).
"""
function add_state!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, state::E, prob::T=zero(T)) where {E,T}
    haskey(sp.index, state) && return sp
    push!(sp.states, state)
    push!(sp.probs, prob)
    sp.index[state] = length(sp.states)
    if !haskey(sp.global_id, state)
        sp.global_id[state] = sp.next_id
        push!(sp.id_to_state, state)
        sp.next_id += 1
    end
    sp
end

"""
    remove_states!(space, mask)

Remove states where `mask[i] == true`. Rebuild compact index.
"""
function remove_states!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, remove_mask::BitVector) where {E,T}
    keep = .!remove_mask
    sp.states = sp.states[keep]
    sp.probs = sp.probs[keep]
    empty!(sp.index)
    for (i, s) in enumerate(sp.states)
        sp.index[s] = i
    end
    sp
end

"""
    expand!(space, model, bc; depth=1)

Add stoichiometric neighbors of all current states that satisfy `bc`.
Probabilities of new states are initialized to zero.
"""
function expand!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    for _ in 1:depth
        current = copy(sp.states)
        for x in current
            for ν in model.stoichvecs
                y = x + ν
                if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
                    add_state!(sp, y)
                end
            end
        end
    end
    sp
end

"""
    expand_ssa!(space, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

Legacy SSA-style expansion: for each active state, sample one reaction by
propensity and add the sampled successor if it satisfies `bc`.
"""
function expand_ssa!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    n_rxn == 0 && return sp

    for _ in 1:depth
        current = copy(sp.states)
        for x in current
            props = Vector{Float64}(undef, n_rxn)
            total = 0.0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                α = Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
                α = max(0.0, α)
                props[k] = α
                total += α
            end
            total <= 0 && continue

            threshold = rand() * total
            csum = 0.0
            chosen = 0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                csum += props[k]
                if threshold <= csum
                    chosen = k
                    break
                end
            end
            chosen == 0 && continue

            y = x + model.stoichvecs[chosen]
            if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
                add_state!(sp, y)
            end
        end
    end
    sp
end

"""
    compress!(space, model, rates, t, prob_quantile; flux_tolerance=1e-6)

Flux-aware pruning with legacy count-quantile candidate selection.

Candidates are chosen by state count:
`round(prob_quantile * n_states)` lowest-probability states.
If `flux_tolerance <= 0`, all candidates are pruned.
Returns `(total_flux, n_removed)`.
"""
function compress!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real,
                   prob_quantile::Real; flux_tolerance::Real=1e-6) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return (zero(T), 0)

    # Compute flux for each state: p(x) * sum_k a_k(x)
    flux = Vector{T}(undef, n)
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        w = zero(T)
        for prop in model.propensities
            w += prop(sp.states[i], rates, t)
        end
        flux[i] = sp.probs[i] * w
    end
    total_flux = sum(flux)
    flux_threshold = total_flux * flux_tolerance

    idx = sortperm(sp.probs)
    n_remove = round(Int, clamp(prob_quantile, 0, 1) * n)
    candidates = n_remove > 0 ? idx[1:min(n_remove, n)] : Int[]

    remove_mask = falses(n)
    n_removed = 0
    if flux_tolerance <= 0
        for i in candidates
            remove_mask[i] = true
            n_removed += 1
        end
    else
        for i in candidates
            if flux[i] < flux_threshold
                remove_mask[i] = true
                n_removed += 1
            end
        end
    end

    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
    (total_flux, n_removed)
end

"""
    prune_threshold!(space, threshold; max_probs=nothing)

Simple threshold-based pruning: remove states whose probability (or lookback-window
max probability, if `max_probs` is provided) is below `threshold`.
Returns the number of states removed.
"""
function prune_threshold!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, threshold::Real;
                          max_probs::Union{Nothing, Dict{E,<:Real}}=nothing) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return 0
    remove_mask = falses(n)
    n_removed = 0
    for i in 1:n
        p = max_probs !== nothing ? get(max_probs, sp.states[i], sp.probs[i]) : sp.probs[i]
        if p < threshold
            remove_mask[i] = true
            n_removed += 1
        end
    end
    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
    n_removed
end

"""
    renormalize!(space)

Scale probabilities so they sum to 1. Returns the sum before normalization.
"""
function renormalize!(sp::StateSpace)
    s = sum(sp.probs)
    if s > 0
        sp.probs ./= s
    end
    s
end

"""
    get_global_ids(space) -> Vector{Int}

Return the global IDs of the current active states (in compact order).
"""
function get_global_ids(sp::StateSpace)
    [sp.global_id[s] for s in sp.states]
end

max probability, if `max_probs` is provided) is below `threshold`.
Returns the number of states removed.
"""
function prune_threshold!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, threshold::Real;
                          max_probs::Union{Nothing, Dict{E,<:Real}}=nothing) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return 0
    remove_mask = falses(n)
    n_removed = 0
    for i in 1:n
        p = max_probs !== nothing ? get(max_probs, sp.states[i], sp.probs[i]) : sp.probs[i]
        if p < threshold
            remove_mask[i] = true
            n_removed += 1
        end
    end
    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
    n_removed
end

"""
    renormalize!(space)

Scale probabilities so they sum to 1. Returns the sum before normalization.
"""
function renormalize!(sp::StateSpace)
    s = sum(sp.probs)
    if s > 0
        sp.probs ./= s
    end
    s
end

"""
    get_global_ids(space) -> Vector{Int}

Return the global IDs of the current active states (in compact order).
"""
function get_global_ids(sp::StateSpace)
    [sp.global_id[s] for s in sp.states]
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control parameter.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.
- `dt_max::Float64 = Inf`: Per-depth-unit time step cap: `1/λ_downstream`,
  where `λ_downstream` is the exit rate of the fast downstream states first
  reached by expansion. The actual cap applied is `expansion_depth * dt_max`,
  so increasing expansion depth automatically relaxes the cap proportionally.
  Required for slow-start systems where `Φ_out → 0` at `t=0` (e.g. the
  Bottleneck system), which would otherwise produce a single giant step.
  Set `dt_max = 1/λ_downstream`; leave as `Inf` if the flux step is
  already sufficient (κ = λ_max/Φ_out ≤ 1/ε_dt throughout).

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ,  expansion_depth * dt_max,  tf - t)

where `Φ = Σᵢ pᵢ·wᵢ` is the probability-weighted internal exit rate (compressed
generator diagonal). For stoichiometric expansion all neighbors are in J so Φ ≈ Φ_total
and the bound `‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt ≈ Φ·dt = ε_dt` (Corollary 4.7) holds directly.
For SSA expansion (e.g. Oregonator) Φ < Φ_total, but Φ still tracks instantaneous
system activity and gives empirically good adaptive control.
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
    expand_method::Symbol = :stoich
    dt_max::Float64 = Inf
    # Optional progress callback: called every save_interval steps with
    # (t_current, t_log, mean_trajectory_matrix).  Use terminal_progress()
    # to get a live UnicodePlots display in the terminal.
    progress_callback = nothing
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics

Per-step diagnostic data from an AdaptiveFSP solve.

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.
- `t_log`: simulated time after each iteration.
- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `flux_log`: internal flux `Φ = Σᵢ pᵢ·wᵢ` (compressed generator diagonal) at each iteration.
- `total_iters`: total number of iterations executed.
"""
struct AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics
    dt_log::Vector{Float64}
    t_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    flux_log::Vector{Float64}
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ_total`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log        = Float64[]
    t_log         = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]
    flux_log      = Float64[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow, exit_rate_boundary =
            reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step: dt = min(ε_dt/Φ, d·dt_max, tf-t)
        # Φ = Σᵢ p[i]·(internal exit rate at xᵢ) = -dot(diag(A), p).
        # For stoichiometric expansion Φ ≈ Φ_total (all neighbors in J, Φ_out≈0),
        # so ‖ε‖₁ ≲ Φ_total·dt ≈ Φ·dt = ε_dt (Corollary 4.7).
        # For SSA expansion Φ < Φ_total (only 1 neighbor per state in J), but Φ
        # still tracks system activity and gives empirically good step control.
        Φ = dot(-LinearAlgebra.diag(A), sp.probs)
        dt_flux = Φ > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt_flux, alg.expansion_depth * alg.dt_max, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))
        push!(flux_log, Φ)

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
            if !isnothing(alg.progress_callback)
                partial = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
                extra = (step_t=t_log, dt_log=dt_log, size_log=size_log_diag, flux_log=flux_log)
                alg.progress_callback(t, sol_t, mean_trajectory(partial), extra)
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol  = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics(dt_log, t_log, size_log_diag, flux_log, iter)
    (sol, diag)
end
